topic: What a loan against mutual funds is
content: A loan against mutual funds (LAMF) lets you pledge your mutual fund units as security and borrow money. Your units are not sold: they stay invested and continue to gain or lose with the market. Pledged units cannot be redeemed until the loan is repaid or the pledge is released.
Loan against mutual funds on Groww is available at 10.5% per annum. Interest = amount used x 10.5% x days used / 365. Example: ₹10,000 used for 1 month costs about ₹88 in interest.
notes: Rate given by case-study brief; confirm in app

content: Lenders typically lend up to about 50% of the value of equity mutual funds and up to about 80% of debt mutual funds. The exact limit depends on the fund and the lender.
notes: Verify Groww's current LTV in app

content: Groww's loan limit against mutual funds has a 12-month tenure and can be renewed without repaying the principal.
Groww says it has no hidden charges. Third-party reviews list no foreclosure or prepayment charges; a processing fee may apply. Check the current fee schedule in the app before applying.

If the value of pledged units falls so that the loan exceeds the allowed limit (e.g. 50% of value), the lender asks you to repay part of the loan or pledge more units. If you don't, the lender can sell pledged units to recover the shortfall.
You can choose which funds and how many units to pledge rather than pledging your whole portfolio.
A loan against mutual funds is a credit product. Repaying on time is reported normally; missed payments can lower your credit score.

Holding ₹52,129 (invested ₹46,997, gain ₹5,132). Need ₹20,000. REDEEM (assuming units under 1 year): exit load 1% = ₹200, short-term tax 20% + 4% cess on the gain portion = about ₹410; total cost about ₹610, and those units stop growing. LOAN at 10.5% p.a.: interest ₹175 for 1 month, ₹525 for 3 months, ₹1,050 for 6 months, ₹2,100 for 12 months; units stay invested. Break-even: over 12 months the loan comes out ahead only if the fund returns more than about 7.5% in that year. Repaid within about 3 months, the loan interest (₹525) is lower than the redemption cost (₹610) even if the market is flat. If units are older than 1 year, redemption has no exit load and long-term gains up to ₹1.25 lakh/year are tax-free, so the loan's cost advantage mostly disappears.
notes: Illustrative; actual exit load/tax depend on each SIP instalment's date

content: For ₹20,000 over 12 months (loan interest ₹2,100 vs redemption cost ₹610): if the fund rises 15%, the kept units gain ₹3,000, net ₹900 with the loan vs -₹610 with redemption. If the fund is flat, net -₹2,100 with the loan. If the fund falls 15%, net -₹5,100 with the loan. With a ₹20,000 loan on a fully pledged ₹52,129 holding at 50% LTV, a fall of about 23% would trigger a margin shortfall.
Credit card revolving interest in India is commonly around 36-42% per year, far higher than 10.5%. On ₹20,000 for 3 months, 36% p.a. would cost about ₹1,800 vs ₹525 at 10.5%.
notes: Credit card rate varies by issuer

content: Motilal Oswal Midcap Fund charges 1% exit load if units are redeemed within 365 days of allotment; nil after 365 days. For SIPs, each instalment is checked separately.
source_name: Groww fund page / Motilal Oswal SID

content: Units are redeemed first-in, first-out: the oldest units are sold first. In a partial redemption, older units (often past the exit-load period and long-term for tax) are used first.

Equity funds: gains on units held up to 12 months are short-term, taxed at 20%; held over 12 months are long-term, taxed at 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh per financial year (limit is per person across all equity holdings). Surcharge and 4% cess apply. Rates unchanged in Budget 2026; section numbers changed under Income Tax Act 2025.
No TDS is deducted on mutual fund capital gains for resident individuals; tax is paid via advance tax or ITR. TDS applies to NRIs.
STT of 0.001% applies on redemption of equity fund units. Stamp duty applies on purchase, not on redemption.

Redemption requests before 3:00 PM on a business day get that day's NAV; later requests get the next business day's NAV. Equity fund proceeds usually reach the registered bank account in 2-3 working days.

You can redeem a specific amount or number of units; the rest stays invested and keeps compounding. Because oldest units go first, partial redemptions often avoid exit load and fall under long-term tax.
A Systematic Withdrawal Plan pays out a fixed amount at regular intervals while the rest stays invested. Each payout is a redemption for exit load and tax.

A Systematic Transfer Plan moves a fixed amount regularly from one scheme to another in the same fund house, e.g. gradually from equity to a lower-volatility fund. Each transfer is a redemption for exit load and tax.
The ₹1.25 lakh long-term gains exemption resets every financial year (April-March). Spreading large redemptions across years can keep more gains tax-free.
Switching to another fund is a redemption plus a new purchase; exit load and capital-gains tax apply.
Pausing or stopping a SIP only stops future instalments. Existing units stay invested.

topic: Loss frequency falls with time (Nifty 50 TRI)
content: Nifty 50 TRI since June 1999 (data to 30 Sep 2026): share of periods with negative returns was about 24% for 1-year holding periods, about 6% for 3 years, about 0.1% for 5 years, and 0% for 7 years or more.
notes: Backtest on one index; past performance

topic: Range of outcomes narrows with time (Nifty 50 TRI)
content: Rolling annualised returns of Nifty 50 TRI since June 1999: 1-year average ~16% (worst -55%, best +108%); 5-year average ~15% (worst -1%); 10-year average ~14% (worst +5%, best +22%).
Nifty Midcap 150 TRI annualised returns as of 30 Sep 2026: 1 year -0.6%, 3 years 6.4%, 5 years 14.2%, 10 years 17.6%. Short periods can be flat or negative; longer periods have been much stronger.
source_name: Baroda BNP Paribas Mid Cap Fund factsheet (benchmark data)

content: A study found that in 8 out of 10 decade-long periods, midcap funds generated over 15% annualised returns.
source_name: Business Today - midcap funds decade-long study

topic: Cost of missing the best days
content: Nifty 50 TRI, April 2005 to July 2026: staying fully invested gave 13.67% a year (15.4x). Missing just the 5 best days cut this to 11.31% (9.8x); missing the 10 best days cut it to 9.75% (7.3x).
source_name: ShareIndia - best and worst days (Nifty 50 TRI)

topic: Best days come right after worst days
content: Seven of the Nifty 50's 10 best days occurred within two weeks of its 10 worst days, so exiting during a fall often means missing the rebound.
source_name: Business Today - Rs 10 lakh in Nifty since 1999

content: The Nifty 50 fell about 38% between mid-January and late March 2020 (Covid crash) and was back above its pre-crash level by the end of 2020.

Midcap funds invest mainly in companies ranked 101-250 by market capitalisation and are labelled Very High risk on the SEBI riskometer. They can fall more than large caps in downturns, but hold many companies, so they are diversified.
The +10.92% on the holding card is an absolute return. For SIPs, XIRR (annualised, accounting for each instalment's date) is the fairer measure.
When prices fall, each SIP instalment buys more units (rupee-cost averaging), which can lower the average cost per unit.
If ₹52,129 grew at an assumed 12% a year it would be about ₹91,869 in 5 years and ₹1,61,905 in 10 years; at 8% a year, about ₹76,595 and ₹1,12,543. Assumed rates are illustrations, not predictions.
Mutual fund units are held in your own folio with the fund house (AMC) and its registrar, not by the app. You can verify them via a Consolidated Account Statement from CAMS, KFintech or MF Central.
Issues can be raised with Groww support first, then the AMC, then on SEBI SCORES.
A capital gains statement can be downloaded from Groww reports, CAMS, KFintech or MF Central.
Only SEBI-registered investment advisers (RIAs) can give personalised investment advice; registration can be checked on the SEBI website.
Units from a recent SIP instalment appear after allotment, usually 1-2 working days after the debit, and can only be redeemed once allotted.
